# Codegen + runtime contract

## What gets emitted

For each `.soql` file, soqlc emits one `.ts` file in the configured `out`
directory. Given:

```sql
-- name: GetAccountById :one
SELECT Id, Name, Industry, AnnualRevenue
FROM Account
WHERE Id = :id;
```

…the generator produces (roughly):

```ts
// Code generated by soqlc. DO NOT EDIT.
import type { SoqlClient } from "@soqlc/runtime";
import { bindParams } from "@soqlc/runtime";

export const GetAccountByIdQuery =
  `SELECT Id, Name, Industry, AnnualRevenue FROM Account WHERE Id = :id`;

export interface GetAccountByIdArgs {
  id: string;
}

export interface GetAccountByIdRow {
  Id: string;
  Name: string;
  Industry?: "Tech" | "Finance" | "Healthcare";
  AnnualRevenue?: number;
}

export async function getAccountById(
  client: SoqlClient,
  args: GetAccountByIdArgs,
): Promise<GetAccountByIdRow | null> {
  const soql = bindParams(GetAccountByIdQuery, args);
  const result = await client.query<GetAccountByIdRow>(soql);
  return result.records[0] ?? null;
}
```

- `:one` returns `Promise<Row | null>` (`records[0] ?? null`).
- `:many` returns `Promise<Row[]>` (just `records`).

The function name is the query header name, camel-cased. The interfaces use
the original PascalCase (so `GetAccountByIdArgs`, `GetAccountByIdRow`).

## Runtime contract

Generated code imports two things from `@soqlc/runtime`:

```ts
export interface SoqlQueryResult<T> {
  totalSize: number;
  done: boolean;
  nextRecordsUrl?: string;
  records: T[];
}

export interface SoqlClient {
  query<T>(soql: string, options?: { tooling?: boolean }): Promise<SoqlQueryResult<T>>;
  queryMore?<T>(nextRecordsUrl: string): Promise<SoqlQueryResult<T>>;
}

export function bindParams(soql: string, args: Record<string, unknown>): string;
```

You provide the `SoqlClient`. Adapters for jsforce, `@salesforce/core`, and
plain `fetch` are easy to write because the interface is so small.

## `bindParams` substitution rules

`bindParams("WHERE Foo = :x", { x: <value> })` substitutes `:x` based on the
JS value's type:

| JS value | Rendered as |
|---|---|
| `string` | `'<value>'` with `'` → `''` and `\` → `\\` |
| `number`, `bigint` | the number literal |
| `boolean` | `true` / `false` |
| `null` or `undefined` | `null` |
| `Date` | ISO 8601 string (unquoted) |
| `Array<T>` | `(<elem>, <elem>, ...)` — each element rendered by the same rules |
| anything else | `JSON.stringify`'d and quoted; a warning is logged |

Identifiers like date literal tokens (`TODAY`, `LAST_N_DAYS:30`) are part of
the SOQL source, not parameters — don't pass them through `bindParams`.

## Driver adapters (not generated; example sketches)

A jsforce adapter:

```ts
import jsforce from "jsforce";
const conn = new jsforce.Connection({ accessToken, instanceUrl });
const client: SoqlClient = {
  query: (soql) => conn.query(soql),
};
```

A `fetch` adapter (Salesforce REST):

```ts
const client: SoqlClient = {
  async query(soql) {
    const url = `${instanceUrl}/services/data/v60.0/query?q=${encodeURIComponent(soql)}`;
    const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` } });
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(await res.text());
    return res.json();
  },
};
```

Both adapters compose with the same generated query functions.
